clue.text: Crime close to cricket grounds

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is taken

parts.note: T is the final letter of cricket
grounds for an action are its reason

explanation.surface: A cricket field is the scene of some offence committed near the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to cricket' looks like a fielding position near the batsman; here it means the last letter of cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the offence of betraying one's country, a serious criminal act.

clue.text: Spinning beast is leaving a naturalist dizzy

indicators.note: the letters of is are leaving, taken away from the fodder
dizzy suggests a whirl, so the remaining letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A naturalist reels away from some creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is leaving' takes IS out of A NATURALIST, and 'dizzy' tells you to rearrange the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarantula is a large hairy spider, a creature that spins silk.

clue.text: Cutting more crust at the sides

parts.note: extra means more

indicators.note: only the letters at the sides of the word, its first and last, are used

parts.note: C and T are the letters at either side of crust

explanation.surface: Trimming off additional crust around the edges of a loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract is a passage taken from a text, like a newspaper cutting.

clue.text: Drink, say, accompanying good food

parts.note: Scotch is whisky
eg, for example, is signalled by say

explanation.surface: A drink, perhaps, to go with something tasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scotch egg is a hard-boiled egg wrapped in sausage meat and breadcrumbs, a British snack.

clue.text: Stupefied maiden's broken heart

indicators.note: the heart word is broken open by the maiden going inside

parts.note: the nub is the heart of a matter
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young woman left dazed by heartbreak.
explanation.definitionFit: Numb means deprived of feeling, dazed or stunned.

clue.text: BNP leader organises marches

indicators.note: the leader of BNP is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter taken
to organise things is to order them

explanation.surface: The head of a far-right party arranges street demonstrations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes the first letter of BNP. 'marches' looks like protest parades; it is the old noun for frontier lands, as in the Welsh Marches.
explanation.definitionFit: Marches are frontier regions between two countries, the same as borderlands.

clue.text: Ill-treated prior fed by Merlin, perhaps

indicators.note: letters that are ill-treated get knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A wizard abuses a monk he has been feeding, in Arthurian style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill-treated' rearranges PRIOR FED BY. Merlin suggests the wizard; it is the small falcon.
explanation.definitionFit: A merlin is a small falcon, so it is one example of a hunting raptor.

clue.text: Pan put in the oven

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to criticise harshly, as a reviewer pans a play
second meaning: to cook meat in the oven

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pan' looks like a cooking pot; it is the verb meaning to criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast is both to slate someone severely and to cook food with dry heat.

clue.text: Energy provided in risky unfinished building

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: the provided word goes in the shortened risky word
the risky word loses its final letter

parts.note: dicey means risky
if means provided, on condition that

explanation.surface: Energy supply in a dangerous half-built structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' looks like part of the half-built building picture, but it only trims the last letter off the word for risky before 'provided' goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large imposing structure.

clue.text: Britpop band did rock vocal

indicators.note: vocal means spoken, so the word is as it would be heard

parts.note: swayed means did rock, moved to and fro

explanation.surface: A 1990s band played rock with singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' suggests music; here it means to sway, and 'vocal' says SWAYED is said aloud. Suede were a leading 1990s British indie band.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede were one of the founding groups of the 1990s Britpop movement.

clue.text: Helping save the last 5 per cent, say

indicators.note: save means except, so the word is taken except its last letter

parts.note: a ration is a helping or portion of food

explanation.surface: Someone saving a final small share of a helping, perhaps for later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save the last' looks like keeping something back; 'save' means 'except', so RATION loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A percentage such as five in a hundred is one way of expressing a proportion between two numbers.

clue.text: Spread made from sea fish parts

indicators.note: the fish parts, or splits, the sea word in two by sitting inside it

parts.note: marine means of the sea
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A bread spread apparently manufactured out of bits of sea fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Margarine is a butter substitute that people spread on bread.

clue.text: Subtlety is not shown in irritation

indicators.note: the word is is not shown inside the longer word, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a nuisance is an irritation

explanation.surface: A remark that subtlety does not come across when someone is irritated.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a fine shade of meaning, a subtle distinction.

clue.text: Common criminal goes before showing remorse

indicators.note: the criminal's word is placed in front of the common one

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
trite means common or hackneyed

explanation.surface: An ordinary crook appears in front of a court looking sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes before' suggests appearing in court, but it simply sets the order of the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrite describes someone feeling and displaying sorrow for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Shortening time on course by acting badly

parts.note: a run is a course, as in a ski run

indicators.note: acting done badly is jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor's poor performance cut short his time on a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Truncating means cutting off part of something to make it shorter.

clue.text: The BBC putting out a release

indicators.note: putting out the letter a means removing it from the word

parts.note: Auntie, or Auntie Beeb, is the affectionate British nickname for the BBC

explanation.surface: The broadcaster issuing a press release.
explanation.walkthrough: The BBC is Britain's public broadcaster, nicknamed Auntie; 'putting out' suggests broadcasting but here means removing the A.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie something is to free or loosen it, so the verb means release.

clue.text: Special forces, fitting in relaxation, briefly recover

indicators.note: the forces fit inside the shortened relaxation word
briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: rest is relaxation
posses are bodies of men specially summoned to enforce the law

explanation.surface: Elite troops squeeze in a quick break before recovering something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special forces' suggests the SAS, but it is POSSES, specially raised forces of men; 'briefly' cuts REST to RES, and POSSES goes 'fitting in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To repossess goods is to take them back, the sense of recovering property when payments lapse.

clue.text: Really a time of popular music or drama

parts.note: so means really, as in so good
pop is popular music
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A wondering remark about an age of pop music or theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a serialised television or radio drama about ordinary lives.

clue.text: Most effective society got rents changed

indicators.note: the letters of got rents are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A landlord's association made the most of altered rents.
explanation.definitionFit: Strongest means the most powerful, the one with greatest effect.

clue.text: Island church admits error defending pride

indicators.note: the island and church let the error inside them

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde, Scotland
CE is the Church of England
OG is an own goal, a defender's error in football

explanation.surface: A Scottish island church lets in a defensive error out of pride.
explanation.walkthrough: ARRAN plus CE 'admits' OG; an own goal (OG) is when a defender puts the ball in their own net.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrogance is an excessive sense of one's own importance, a form of pride.

clue.text: Back receiving pass could be better prepared

indicators.note: the back word receives the other inside it

parts.note: the rear is the back
to pass away is to die

explanation.surface: A rugby or football back taking a pass might be in better shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass' suggests a ball game; here it means pass away, DIE, which REAR is 'receiving'.
explanation.definitionFit: Readier is the comparative of ready, more fully prepared.

clue.text: Moving around a prison

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Someone walking around inside a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means up and about, in motion or out of bed.

clue.text: Minor hearing about sex

indicators.note: the hearing goes about, around, the number

parts.note: a trial is a court hearing
sex is Latin for six, VI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A court case concerning a sexual matter involving a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor' looks like a child in the courtroom picture; it is the adjective meaning unimportant. TRIAL goes 'about' VI.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivial means of little importance, petty or slight.

clue.text: Race winners drew late criticism

definitions.note: describes the result where two runners tie, a noun phrase for that tie

parts.note: the late person is dead
heat is fierce criticism, as in taking the heat

explanation.surface: Runners who finished level, then criticism arriving afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead heat is a race in which two or more competitors finish exactly level.

clue.text: Drank heavily around bus station

indicators.note: around means the word is turned the other way

parts.note: toped means drank heavily

explanation.surface: Someone boozing near the bus terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a garage or terminus where buses are kept.

clue.text: Country hotel fine to host relations

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the fine word hosts the relations word inside it

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, fine, written here as AI
it is a euphemism for sexual relations

explanation.surface: A country hotel that is happy to accommodate family members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relations' suggests relatives, but it means sexual relations, coyly called 'it'; A1, first-rate, is written with the letter I standing in for the figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiti is a Caribbean nation on the island of Hispaniola.

clue.text: Love drug in bottles?

parts.note: pot is cannabis

indicators.note: the word in bottles, or holds inside it, the love letter

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: An aphrodisiac sold in bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a piece of the wordplay, not a link word: it is the word that 'bottles' the love letter. Read as a whole, the clue also describes a love potion.
explanation.definitionFit: A potion is a liquid medicine or magic draught, as with a love potion kept in a flask.

clue.text: Latest letters from Greece to an auditor

indicators.note: to a listener, so the word is as heard

parts.note: nu is a Greek letter, so the plural is nus

explanation.surface: Letters posted from Greece to an accountant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' suggests an accountant; 'to an auditor' means as heard by a listener, so NUS is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: The news is the most recent information about events.

clue.text: Crude publicity one university writer has

parts.note: PR is public relations, publicity
I is the Roman numeral one
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
the writer saying 'I have' gives I've

explanation.surface: A writer at a university has some crude publicity material.
explanation.definitionFit: Primitive means simple and unrefined, the sense of rough or crude.

clue.text: Upper class in crime literature

indicators.note: the answer sits in the run of letters of crime literature

parts.note: the letters run across the end of crime and the start of literature

explanation.surface: Posh people featuring in detective fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the select top layer of society.

clue.text: Any number a mathematician keeps changing

indicators.note: the mathematician keeps the number inside his name

parts.note: Alan Turing was the British mathematician and codebreaker
N stands for any number in algebra

explanation.surface: A mathematician repeatedly alters some figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning means becoming or transforming, as in leaves turning brown.

clue.text: Claret's fabulous colour

indicators.note: fabulous means fanciful or invented, so these letters take on a new form

explanation.surface: Praise for the wonderful hue of a red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a brilliant red hue.
